newsitem.title: PERU: Newshounds adopt "Cerpa" the dog at Peru siege.
newsitem.headline: Newshounds adopt "Cerpa" the dog at Peru siege.

text.p: The world's media camped out at the Lima hostage siege have adopted a stray dog as a mascot, whose aversion to Peruvian police has earned him the nickname "Cerpa" after the Marxist rebel leader.
"He only has to see a policeman go by (and) his hair stands on end and he starts barking madly," Claudia Daut, a Reuters photographer said on Sunday.
And like his namesake -- Nestor Cerpa Cartolini -- the irascible dog is media-friendly.

Feeding the mut's taste for take-out pizza has secured the dog's loyalty for the journalists, who fuss over the black and white stray as he eats, drinks and sleeps alongside them at their stakeout, Daut added.
Rebel leader Cerpa led an audacious attack of 15 heavily armed Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels on the Japanese ambassador's residence on Dec. 17, taking more than 500 hostages.

Cerpa the dog has not been the only canine celebrity. A shell-shocked German shepherd named Emma padded out of the compound to the glare of photographers' flashes after spending 16 lonely days in the diplomatic residence's garden following the assault. Her puppy was believed to have been killed by a bullet during shooting in the initial attack.
